1.title: Understand waste streams and remediation
1.intro: Waste comes as household, business, construction and hazardous streams. Remediation cleans contaminated land or water.
pts: Know the hierarchy: reduce, reuse, recycle, recover, dispose.
Measure a stream: tonnes, composition, sources.
Pick a niche: construction waste, organics, e-waste, site clean-up.
1.ex: A building site produces 60 t of waste; sorting could divert 70% (42 t) from landfill.
1.act: Sample and weigh a waste stream.

2.title: Know environmental and handling rules
pts: Provincial approvals are required for waste handling, transport and processing.
Hazardous waste needs manifests and licensed carriers.
Contaminated sites follow assessment and clean-up standards with qualified professionals.
Worker safety training and protective gear are mandatory.
2.ex: Row: 'Haul hazardous waste | provincial environment ministry | licence and manifest | each load | manifest copies'.

3.title: Plan collection, sorting and treatment
pts: Route collection; sort at source if possible.
Design the sorting line and storage.
3.ex: Contamination 18% in mixed load; with source sorting 6%.

4.title: Cost per tonne and revenue
pts: Revenue: collection fee, gate fee, material sales.
4.ex: Price 180 per tonne; cost 120; margin 60; fixed cost 540,000 a year → 9,000 t. Teaching figures in CAD.
4.act: Build a cost sheet with price fall.

7.title: Manage contamination, community and liability risk
7.ex: Risk: 'Storage fire | 2 x 5 | spacing, detection | site lead | monthly'.

8.title: Pilot a stream
pts: Stop rule: contamination over 15% means fix.

quiz: Clean-up cost if the operator fails.
Spills and fires need quick response.
